conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that the claim that whole-body vibration therapy prevents fractures in osteoporosis sufferers is not well-supported by current evidence and lacks conclusive proof.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
## Conclusion: The Evidence Does Not Clearly Support "Yes"

Your assumption that whole-body vibration (WBV) therapy is effective for preventing fractures in osteoporosis sufferers is **not well-supported** by the current evidence. The findings are mixed, and major reviews urge caution.

### Key Evidence

- A **2017 systematic review and meta-analysis** (Jepsen et al., *BMJ Open*) found that WBV reduces fall rates but "seems to have no overall effect on BMD or microarchitecture," and concluded that "the impact of WBV on fractures requires further larger adequately powered studies." This means the direct fracture-prevention evidence is insufficient. ([https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/7/12/e018342](https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/7/12/e018342))

- A **2022 systematic review** found WBV reduced fracture risk in *healthy* individuals without chronic illnesses, and *may* help as a supplementary treatment — but this is not the same as demonstrating efficacy in confirmed osteoporosis patients. ([https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0965229922000139](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0965229922000139))

- The **2011 Annals of Internal Medicine "State of the Science" review** noted that WBV platforms are **not FDA-approved** for medical purposes and that claims about prevention/treatment of osteoporosis "cannot be made without further research." ([https://www.academia.edu/15191536/Review_Annals_of_Internal_Medicine_Whole_Body_Vibration_Therapy_for_Osteoporosis_State_of_the_Science](https://www.academia.edu/15191536/Review_Annals_of_Internal_Medicine_Whole_Body_Vibration_Therapy_for_Osteoporosis_State_of_the_Science))

- The **UK's Royal Osteoporosis Society** states plainly: "Research also isn't clear if vibration therapy can reduce the risk of broken bones," noting most studies involve people *without* osteoporosis. ([https://theros.org.uk/information-and-support/treatments-and-medicines/complementary-therapies-for-bone-health/vibration-therapy/](https://theros.org.uk/information-and-support/treatments-and-medicines/complementary-therapies-for-bone-health/vibration-therapy/))

### Bottom Line

WBV shows promise for reducing falls (an indirect fracture risk factor), but there is **no conclusive evidence** that it directly prevents fractures in people with osteoporosis. Larger, adequately powered trials are needed before it can be recommended for that purpose.
